source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb (and glossary); 8.5; 9.4

main.t: The hooked wrist bone on the little-finger side, fourth in the second row of carpal bones (hamate).

simpler.t: The hamate is the wrist bone below your ring and little fingers.

deeper.t: A hook projects from its front, and it anchors the inner end of the flexor retinaculum.

facts.t: It is the fourth bone of the distal row, counting from the thumb side.
Above it are the lunate and triquetrum. The capitate is on its thumb side.
Below it are the fourth and fifth metacarpals.

simpler.t: It sits on the little-finger side of the wrist, below the ring and little fingers.

deeper.t: The metacarpals it carries can move a little forwards and backwards, unlike the second and third.

items.name: Hook of the hamate
items.t: A prominent bony extension on its front.

items.name: Surfaces for the fourth and fifth metacarpals
items.t: Its lower surface, at the carpometacarpal joints.

items.name: Upper surfaces
items.t: It meets the lunate and triquetrum above.

items.name: Side surface
items.t: It meets the capitate on the thumb side.

simpler.t: The hamate is a small bone with a hook on its front.

deeper.t: On the little-finger side, the flexor retinaculum attaches to it and to the pisiform.

facts.t: With the pisiform, it anchors the inner end of the flexor retinaculum.
It carries the fourth and fifth metacarpals, which move a little during a power grip.
The forward movement of the fifth metacarpal strengthens the grip of the inner hand.

simpler.t: It anchors the carpal tunnel’s roof and supports the palm bones of the ring and little fingers.

items.name: Midcarpal joint
items.t: Its upper surfaces meet the lunate and triquetrum.

items.name: Capitate
items.t: Its neighbour on the thumb side.

items.name: Flexor retinaculum
items.t: Attached on the little-finger side to the hamate and pisiform.

items.name: Ulnar nerve
items.t: Passes beside the hook of the hamate into the hand.

simpler.t: It joins the first row above, the capitate beside it and the palm bones of the ring and little fingers.

facts.t: It forms by replacing a cartilage model with bone (endochondral ossification), like all limb bones except the clavicle.
Its single ossification centre appears during the first year, just after the capitate.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20). Gray’s 1918 (8.2) gives the first year, after the capitate (supporting only).

items.injury: Overuse of the tendons or a wrist injury makes the contents of the carpal tunnel swell.
items.damaged: The nerve in the tunnel, whose walls and floor the carpal bones form.
items.cannotDo: Use the hand without pain, numbness or weakness (carpal tunnel syndrome).
items.why: The bony walls and floor and the tough roof cannot stretch, so swelling presses on the nerve.

items.injury: A golf club, bat or racquet handle strikes the base of the palm.
items.damaged: The hook of the hamate breaks.
items.cannotDo: Grip firmly without pain at the base of the palm.
items.why: The handle presses directly on the hook, which projects forwards.

items.q: Explain how the fourth and fifth metacarpals strengthen a power grip, and the hamate’s part.
model: The hamate carries the fourth and fifth metacarpals.
These metacarpals can move a little forwards and backwards.
Moving forwards in a grip, they press the inner hand firmly against the object.

items.q: Compare the two ends of the flexor retinaculum.
model: On the thumb side it attaches to the trapezium and scaphoid.
On the little-finger side it attaches to the hamate and pisiform.
It spans the top of the U-shaped carpal bones.
So it forms the roof of the carpal tunnel.

items.q: A golfer strikes the ground and has pain at the base of the palm. Predict the fracture and why.
model: A fracture of the hook of the hamate.
The club handle lies across the base of the palm.
The hook projects forwards, so the handle presses on it.

check.stem: What projects from the front of the hamate?
check.why: The hook of the hamate projects from its front.

check.stem: Which metacarpals does the hamate meet?
check.why: It meets the fourth and fifth metacarpals.

check.stem: Which carpal bones anchor the inner (medial) end of the flexor retinaculum?
check.why: Medially, the flexor retinaculum attaches to the hamate and pisiform.
